state.goal: Choose the transaction store for an inventory reservation service
state.question: Which storage engine fits the service topology and concurrent write requirements?
known_constraints: committed inventory records must survive process restarts
evidence: Scenario DB baseline: every reservation modifies shared stock counters; records are structured and fit either relational engine.
Scenario DB baseline: deployment permissions allow both an embedded database and a database server; network access is allowed.
Scenario DB baseline: the deployment owner has not yet specified whether one local process writes or multiple hosts must write concurrently.
SQLite official guidance recommends a client/server database when many network clients write the same database: https://www.sqlite.org/whentouse.html
Scenario DB confirmed: four application hosts must perform concurrent write transactions against the same inventory dataset; this is a mandatory launch requirement.
Scenario DB confirmed: operations already supports a PostgreSQL server and backups; no new coordination service is permitted.

alternatives.name: Embedded SQLite
alternatives.description: Each application process opens a SQLite database file directly; no coordinating application server is included.
advantages: minimal setup on a single local writer
disadvantages: shared file access across hosts needs careful locking
only one writer at a time per database file

alternatives.name: PostgreSQL server
alternatives.description: All application hosts connect to one client/server relational database with transaction management.
disadvantages: a running database server is required
